Both sought national development and progress, but with different focuses.

Self-improvement for wealth corresponds to democracy and republicanism: The Self-Strengthening Movement advocated self-improvement for wealth through technological progress to enhance national power, while the Xinhai Revolution promoted democracy and republicanism through political system reform to achieve national modernization. Both sought national progress, but with different methods and means.

Li Hongzhang corresponds to Sun Yat-sen: Li Hongzhang was the representative figure of the Self-Strengthening Movement who promoted its implementation, while Sun Yat-sen was the leader and soul figure of the Xinhai Revolution. Both were the leaders and representative figures of their respective movements.

The Landlord Class Westernization School corresponds to the bourgeoisie revolutionary faction: The supporters of the Self-Strengthening Movement were primarily the Landlord Class Westernization School who hoped to maintain their own interests through technological reform, while the supporters of the Xinhai Revolution were mainly the bourgeois revolutionary faction who sought to achieve national democracy and modernization by overthrowing the Qing dynasty. Both were the supporters and drivers of their respective movements, but with different class bases and interests.

The feudal ruler self-help movement corresponds the bourgeoisie revolutionary movement: The Self-Strengthening Movement was seen as a self-help movement by the feudal rulers to seek their own survival, while the Xinhai Revolution was a revolutionary movement by the bourgeoisie to achieve national democracy and modernization. Both were social changes in their respective eras, but with different driving forces and purposes.

background.source: The feminist movement, also known as the women's movement, is a social and political campaign that seeks to address discrimination and inequality between men and women. It started in the 1800s and has gone through four high moments or waves of activism. The priorities of the movement range from reproductive rights, domestic violence, equal pay, women's suffrage, sexual harassment, to sexual violence. Different waves of the movement brought in women of different social classes, women of color, and women from other developing nations who were seeking solidarity. Feminism also involves maintaining focus on women's reproductive rights, such as the right to abortion. The Fourth-wave feminism examines the interlocking systems of power that contribute to the social stratification of traditionally marginalized groups, as well as the world around them. Although the movement started in the Western world, its priorities and impacts have expanded globally.
background.target: The Revolution of 1911, also known as the Xinhai Revolution, was a pivotal event in Chinese history that marked the end of the Manchu-led Qing dynasty and kicked off the era of the Democratic Republic of China. After a decade of unrest and activity from various factions, the revolution was sparked by the Wuchang Uprising on 10 October 1911, which quickly spread across the country. Members of the New Army, along with underground anti-Qing groups, revolutionaries in exile, and reformers, renounced the Qing dynasty and demanded change. On 1 January 1912, the National Assembly declared the establishment of the Republic of China, with Sun Yat-sen, the leader of the bourgeois revolutionary movement, as its first President. However, political division and warlordism marred attempts at consolidating a legitimate central government. The ideals of nationalism, republicanism, modernization, and national unity, which the revolution embodied, continue to be celebrated today in both the People's Republic of China and the Republic of China on Taiwan.
